How the predictions work

Each SKU gets one predicted outcome (the most serious problem found) and the error code Azure returns for it. Other problems for the same SKU are listed under Other notes. The order of checks:

OutcomeWhat the script checkedError the customer sees
SKU restrictedaz vm list-skus shows a Location restriction (reason NotAvailableForSubscription, or QuotaId when the subscription offer type can't use that size).SkuNotAvailable (ARM/Bicep validation shows InvalidTemplateDeployment wrapping it)
Family quota is 0 / exceededFamily vCPU limit minus current usage is less than the SKU's vCPUs.OperationNotAllowed or QuotaExceeded, "Operation could not be completed as it results in exceeding approved <family> Cores quota"
Regional quota exceeded"Total Regional vCPUs" free is less than the SKU's vCPUs.Same codes; the message names Total Regional Cores
Zonal deploy fails in zone XA Zone restriction blocks the SKU in some or all zones.SkuNotAvailable "...not available in location 'X' zones 'N'"
Only offered in zone(s) / no zone supportThe SKU is offered in fewer zones than the region has, or in none.SkuNotAvailable only if you pin a zone the SKU isn't in
Quota unknown / tightThe family wasn't in az vm list-usage, or only 1–2 VMs fit.Quota errors when you scale out
Allocation riskRule of thumb only: GPU (N-series), HPC (H-series), M-series, legacy sizes (Av1, Dv1, DSv1, D15_v2, G), very large sizes (64+ vCPUs or 512+ GB), or sizes offered in a single zone.Possible AllocationFailed, ZonalAllocationFailed, OverconstrainedAllocationRequest, OverconstrainedZonalAllocationRequest
Will deployNo restriction and at least one VM fits in both quotas.None expected. Allocation can still fail: Azure doesn't publish free hardware capacity.

Pre-deployment checklist

Run these in Cloud Shell for the exact size, region and subscription you plan to use (values below are filled in from this report; change them as needed):



Tip: validate a whole deployment without creating anything with az deployment group validate (or what-if). It catches SkuNotAvailable and many quota errors before deploy, but not allocation failures.



SKU restricted: SkuNotAvailable


Confirm




Look at the Restrictions column. NotAvailableForSubscription, type: Location means the size is blocked in the whole region for this subscription. type: Zone lists the blocked zones. QuotaId means the subscription's offer type (for example a free trial or some sponsored offers) can't use this size.


Fix


    

  • Pick another size with similar specs that isn't restricted (filter this report by Will deploy and min vCPUs / memory), or another region.
    • 

  • To enable the size: Azure portal > Help + support > Create a support request. Issue type Service and subscription limits (quotas), quota type Compute-VM (cores-vCPUs) subscription limit increases. Choose the region and VM series and give the vCPU limit you need. Microsoft calls this a SKU request.
    • 

  • For QuotaId, the fix is usually a different subscription offer (for example moving from a free trial to pay-as-you-go).
    • 




vCPU quota: OperationNotAllowed / QuotaExceeded


Azure enforces two vCPU quotas per subscription per region, and a VM must fit in both: the VM-family quota (for example "Standard DSv5 Family vCPUs") and Total Regional vCPUs. Spot VMs use a separate "Total Regional Low-priority vCPUs" quota. A family quota of 0 means you must request quota before the first VM.


Confirm




Fix


    

  • Portal: search Quotas > Compute (My quotas), select the family and region > New Quota Request. Or Subscriptions > your subscription > Usage + quotas > Request increase. Many requests are approved automatically within minutes. If it's rejected you get a link to open a support request.
    • 

  • Approving a family increase also raises Total Regional vCPUs if needed. If only the regional quota is short, request a regional increase.
    • 

  • CLI (needs the quota extension; az extension add --name quota):
    • 





  • Or free quota: delete unused VMs. Note that stopped (deallocated) VMs don't count toward vCPU quota, but VMs that are only stopped (still allocated) do.



Zone restrictions and zone-pinned sizes


    

  • A Zone restriction blocks only deployments pinned to those zones (--zone N / zones: ["N"]). Use a zone listed as OK in the outcome. If every zone is restricted, deploy without a zone, or file the same support request as above and name the zones you need.
    • 

  • Some sizes are only offered in some zones (see the Zones column). Pinning a VM to a zone where the size isn't offered fails with SkuNotAvailable. For a zone-redundant design, choose a size that is offered in all the zones you need.
    • 

  • Zone numbers are mapped per subscription: zone "1" in one subscription might not be the same datacenter as zone "1" in another. Check this report for each subscription.
    • 

  • A size with an empty Zones column has no zone support in that region. Deploy it as a regional (non-zonal) VM.
    • 




Allocation failures: AllocationFailed, ZonalAllocationFailed, OverconstrainedAllocationRequest


These mean Azure doesn't have free hardware for the size in that region, zone or cluster right now. Quota and restrictions can be fine. No API shows free capacity ahead of time, so the "Allocation risk" flag is only a hint. Try these fixes in order:


    

  1. Retry later. Capacity frees up as other customers deallocate VMs.
    2. 

  2. Try another size, ideally a newer generation or another size in the same family (for example v5 instead of v3, or an AMD a size instead of Intel). The error message often suggests alternative sizes and zones. Use them.
    3. 

  3. Try another zone, or no zone. A regional (non-zonal) VM can be placed anywhere in the region.
    4. 

  4. Try another region.
    5. 

  5. Remove constraints (Overconstrained* errors): turn off accelerated networking, remove the VM from its proximity placement group, and drop UltraSSD or Premium SSD v2 disks. Each one narrows the hardware Azure can use.
    6. 

  6. Availability sets: resizing, adding VMs, or starting some of the VMs in a set must happen on the cluster that already hosts the set. Stop (deallocate) all VMs in the set, then start them together so Azure can choose any cluster. Or create the new VM in a different availability set.
    7. 

  7. Proximity placement groups: deallocate all VMs in the group, then start the most restrictive size (for example a GPU or M-series VM) first.
    8. 

  8. Scale sets with a single placement group are limited to one cluster. Use singlePlacementGroup=false where your workload allows it.
    9. 

  9. Legacy sizes (Av1, Dv1, DSv1, D15_v2, G) run on older hardware that is shrinking. Move to the current equivalents (Av2, Dv3/Dv5 and so on).
    10. 

  10. Need guaranteed capacity? Use an on-demand capacity reservation (next section).
    11. 






Capacity reservations: guaranteed capacity


An on-demand capacity reservation holds capacity for a given size, count and (optionally) zone. The SLA applies once the reservation succeeds. You pay the pay-as-you-go price for reserved capacity whether or not VMs are using it, and reserved instance discounts can apply to it. Creating the reservation can itself fail if there's no capacity, so create it before you need it. It also uses vCPU quota, and sponsored and free-trial subscriptions can't use it.





Spot VMs aren't a capacity fix


Spot VMs run on spare capacity. Azure can evict them with 30 seconds' notice when it needs the capacity back, and they have no SLA. When a region is short on hardware, Spot capacity is usually the first to go. Spot also uses its own Low-priority vCPU quota. Use Spot for interruptible work, not to get around AllocationFailed.



Other checks before you deploy


    

  • VM generation: "Gen2 images only" in Other notes means the size supports only Generation 2 VMs, so use a Gen2 image. Some sizes are Gen1 only.
    • 

  • Accelerated networking: if a size doesn't support it (see Other notes), turn it off on the NIC or choose another size.
    • 

  • Disks and NICs: the maximum number of data disks and NICs depends on the size. Check the size's docs page.
    • 

  • Resizing a running VM: if the new size isn't available on the current cluster, deallocate the VM first and then resize.
    • 

  • This report is a point-in-time snapshot. Restrictions and quota change, so re-run it before large deployments.
    •

How to read this. Predicted outcome combines SKU restrictions and vCPU quota for this subscription, and links to the matching help topic.
Status: NotAvailable means the SKU is blocked in that region. PartiallyAvailable means it is blocked in some availability zones.
Can deploy 1 is Yes when the SKU isn't restricted and one VM fits in both the family and regional vCPU quota.
Quota is a limit, not a guarantee of physical capacity, so a deployment can still fail with AllocationFailed.
Capacity reservations are the only way to guarantee capacity in advance.
